generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, the plan joins up across a module. You might revise a theory actively by rebuilding it from memory, mix a diagram of a study's design with explaining findings aloud, and test yourself on key experiments. Then you carry that control into the exam, pacing an essay on, say, attachment or memory to the clock. The strands support one another rather than standing apart.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two psychology students revised the cognitive approach for the same exam. One reread the textbook chapter and made no plan for the day, then spent too long on the first essay and rushed the second. The other mapped the models visually, explained the studies aloud, tested herself on the evidence, and sat the exam to a timed plan. Her preparation held together, and her marks rose across both essays.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, active revision works best as one connected plan. You let active learning guide a varied mix of techniques across theories and studies, then carry that control into a timed exam. The joined-up approach, not any single technique, is what lifts your marks.

check.body: A student revises a topic actively, uses a mix of techniques across families, and sits the exam to a calm, timed plan. They do better than on earlier exams. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first report, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next report.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the three strands work together: active revision, a varied technique mix and an exam-day plan form one approach.
_items.feedback: Yes. The strands joined up into one plan, and that is what paid off.

_items.text: That only the exam-day plan made the difference to their result.
_items.feedback: The exam-day plan protected marks, but active revision and the technique mix earned them.

_items.text: That they simply spent far more hours than before.
_items.feedback: The point is the joined-up approach, not extra hours.

_items.text: That the techniques alone, without active learning behind them, improved the result.
_items.feedback: The techniques work because active learning is the principle driving them.
